answer: Each identity builds a vine of receipts on a lagoon ledger, each carrying the previous receipt's hash, so its history is one unbroken vine, and its five starter receipts each carry 40-credit escrow, burned if a link breaks. A prism audit splits each receipt into task, timing and counterpart facets, checked against the ledger; a forged link fails a facet. A rented vine fails: its timing and counterpart facets mismatch the renter's history. The kth fake needs five fresh receipts, so 1,000 fakes pay 200,000 credits, none shared across vines. An honest identity builds one vine and pays once.
